paite: Huan TOUPA thu Jonah kiang ah ahong tung nawn leuleu a,
heading: Jonah Sawl Nawnna Leh Mite Kisikna
english: Yahweh’s word came to Jonah the second time, saying,

paite: "Thou inla, Nineveh khua, khopi thupitak ah hoh inla, thu gen ding ka hon chih pen va tangkoupih in," chi in.
english: “Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and preach to it the message that I give you.”

paite: Huchi in Jonah athou a, TOUPA thu bang in Nineveh ah ahohta hi. Nineveh bel khopi thupi petmah, ni thum pai aching hi.
english: So Jonah arose, and went to Nineveh, according to Yahweh’s word. Now Nineveh was an exceedingly great city, three days’ journey across.

paite: Jonah ni khat pai zoh chiang khopi sung ah ava pai phot a, "Ni sawmli in, Nineveh hihman ahi ding hi," chi in akikou hi.
english: Jonah began to enter into the city a day’s journey, and he cried out, and said, “In forty days, Nineveh will be overthrown!”

paite: Nineveh mite'n Pathian agingta ua; an ngawl apuang ua, alak ua alianpen a kipan aneupen tan in sai-ip puan asilh uhi.
english: The people of Nineveh believed God; and they proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from their greatest even to their least.

paite: Huai thu Nineveh kumpipa bil ahong tungta a, alaltutphah a kipan athou a, akumpi puan asuah a, sai-ip puan silh in, vut ah atuta hi.
english: The news reached the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, took off his royal robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.

paite: Kumpipa leh amiliante thupiak in kumpipa'n Nineveh khosung ah thu apuang in apulakta hi. "Mihing hiam, ganta hiam, ganhon hiam, belamhon hiamte in bangmah chiam kei uhen; banghiam ne in tui leng dawn kei uhen;
english: He made a proclamation and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, “Let neither man nor animal, herd nor flock, taste anything; let them not feed, nor drink water;

paite: mihing leh ganhingte'n sai-ip puan silh uhenla, nakpitak in Pathian sam uhen; ahi, michih in amau lampi hoih lou leh akhut ua hiamgamna lehngatsan uhen.
english: but let them be covered with sackcloth, both man and animal, and let them cry mightily to God. Yes, let them turn everyone from his evil way and from the violence that is in his hands.

paite: I manlouhna ding in, Pathian lunghei in lungsim kilehhei in, ahehna mahmah a kipan akilehhei kei ding chih kua'n ahia theithei?" achi hi.
english: Who knows whether God will not turn and relent, and turn away from his fierce anger, so that we might not perish?”

paite: Huchi in Pathian in athilhihte uh en in, alampi hoih lou uh alehngatsan uh chih amu a; akiang ua achihsa, hih atup thil hoih lou Pathian in alehngatsan a; ahihta kei hi.
english: God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way. God relented of the disaster which he said he would do to them, and he didn’t do it.
